notes: Fine as a very basic exercise. If we wanted it to be better musically, we could use more chord inversions rather than having everything in root position.
Also works for a basic exercise. Like out of a textbook. But also not very musical.
Somewhat boring, could be made more interesting, at the very least by using chord inversions appropriately. For a root position exercise it's good.
The phrasing is poor--using a secondary dominant into V like that in measure 3 of an 8 measure phrase feels off. No intermediate cadence really.

Some of the jumps in the left-hand arpeggios are too big, and that will have a big jump from the last note of one arpeggio to the first note of the next arpeggio. Also, towards the end, the right hand chords, especially the very last chord, spin much too far.

And the chord voicing or the spelling out of the arpeggios in the left-hand of the second to last measure are kind of awkward

I like the melody better than this one. I think that it flows more. I also liked the in measure nine. It had a D in the bass arpeggio, it seems like that was potentially a mistake, but I thought it fit well as a non-chord tone and so I actually liked that.

And I think that that's part of what makes romantic music the way that it is, whereas I feel like both of the other two examples are very diatonic and stick very closely to the harmonies of the chords, which is good and it's a good demonstration of simple music theory.

However, I think both could be better by using more non-chord tones. I do think that the arpeggios worked a little bit better in this one, though they still had issues with the distance or the long jumps from one to the next

I think this is pretty good. Again, I think at a very basic level it demonstrates an understanding of the theory, and it uses some of the techniques. It is kind of bland and basic, so it's a little bit boring in that regard. I will say measure 11, the rhythms seem to be completely off, and I think the way that the triplets are notated is kind of awkward as well.

I think it's something that's typically given in the time signature, and then explicit triplets are marked, but other than that, eighth notes are just assumed to be swung, and so that's one place where I think this could improve at least in the notation.

And then I don't love the voice crossing in the final measure between the melody and the left hand on beat 2. And then the big jump to the last chord is also kind of sudden and strange

I think my feedback on this one is pretty similar. It shows a basic application of the theory and of the techniques, and I think it does a good job making it playable. I also liked the use of the secondary dominant. I thought that was an interesting way to catch.

I noticed some notes that maybe didn't quite fit. For example, measure 3, beat 3, an A natural in the bass with an A flat in the right hand on top of it, and that didn't sound very good.

I also noticed some voice crossing in measure 8 on the downbeat of beat 2, and that didn't sound very good either. And so that's an issue that I don't think would work very well. I liked the use of the repeat, and I thought it was interesting to have a first and second ending.

However, it feels like the first ending measure is kind of building up to something, but there's nothing for it to build up to because then it goes back to the repeat where there's nothing there. So anyways, it works, but and it's an interesting artistic choice

Overall, I was pretty impressed with the harmonic progression of this. I thought the harmonies were really really interesting to listen to, and sometimes actually caught me off guard in a good way, and it was a good surprise that kept me interested and kept me listening rather than bored.

I think the left hand pattern is a little bit boring, and you know it'd be good to have some more variation there, but overall, this is markedly better than the arrangements we've been seeing before

Honestly, I was really impressed with this one. I thought that the structure of the musical piece was actually quite impressive, and I appreciated the repetition. I think that the phrases could have been slightly more uniform and well defined. I don't know, but maybe 12 bar phrases is fine.

It's weird that it was that it's like 5 phrases, though. Anyways, but honestly, I really liked the melody. I thought that it did a great job, you know, being interesting, and I liked the sequence and repetition that was used, and there were some both harmonic and melodic choices that were really interesting and kept me engaged.

I liked this. This is a step up again, I'd say this is pretty simple, and the left hand could be a little bit more interesting, but I think it's nice. I like the stride technique and the alternation of quarter notes and eighth notes, so it's pretty good

Wow, consider me impressed again. Again, I thought that the sequence and repetition was really interesting, and I liked the usage of that. I really liked the descending bass pattern, and I really liked the harmonic progression too. I thought this was actually quite good.

The left hand again could use some variation in terms of the rhythm. And the right hand was pretty repetitive in terms of the rhythm, and so I think there's a little bit more room to branch out. I know that a couple of bars did.

But anyways, there's still some room there. I know that a couple of bars did.

But anyways, there's still some room there. I'm not sure exactly what's going on with the phrasing, but I think it's nice. I really liked in measure 15 how the note in the melody was tied from measure 14.

I thought that was a really cool impact and a really unique choice

This is quite good as well. I think my comments are about the same as on the other pieces. I like the type of sequence and repetition in the right hand and the melody. And I really like the harmonic progression.

It felt very interesting to me. And does feel kind of Chopin-esque. The left hand could use more rhythmic variation. And anyways, yeah, along with some of the others I really liked the choice to have this one in 6-8.

I thought it really worked well, and I felt like it moved very well, and I loved the motion it had to it compared to piece number 1 which was somewhat slow in my opinion

I wasn't quite as impressed with this one. I thought it was alright, and I thought the melody actually did a pretty good job, and I think the harmonic progression is good. However, I think a lot of the voicing choices for the bass arpeggios really are quite poor, and it just feels kind of closely clustered and doesn't feel very clear in a way that a Chopin piece typically does.

And so I think the baseline needs quite a bit of reworking. There were also some cordon versions that I didn't really love. And anyway, I don't know. For arpeggios in this eighth note pattern like this, I don't really love when they're so strictly holding on to the chords.

I think Chopin and Liszt have a lot more freedom in their arpeggios when the left hand is doing them, and I think that this piece could benefit from it. I think it was alright, but it definitely wasn't my favorite, and it's probably my least favorite so far

This one was okay. I didn't necessarily love the melody. I thought there were some interesting parts of it, but I'm not quite sure I don't know that I can put my finger on quite what the issue is. I think the use of the A flats felt a little weird to me, at least in the places where A flat was not a chord tone.

I felt like that was a dissonant and not a good way. And just felt kind of uncomfortable. There was also a double sharp in there that I think was probably a mistake. Anyway, yeah, it was a little weird.

I think this one needs some work. I thought the harmonic ideas were interesting. It was good use of chromaticism. But yeah, I don't know.

It just felt a little bit weird. Like it was cool that we had the chromatic descending bass line in half steps. And then, and then, you know, there were other places where we had the half-step increase and decrease, but like it felt like too non-diatonic, maybe.

I don't know. This one was just a little bit weird. Didn't quite sit well with me. It was interesting, but I don't know that it quite fit Chopin's style. I think that there's merit in this type of music, but I don't know that this is what I was asking for

Big fan of this one. I think it might be my favorite. It did a great job with this sequence and repetition, and I thought the 16th note runs were actually very fun and playful, and I really enjoyed those. It was cool to see the secondary dominant employed in measure 3 and that actually felt like a pretty good application of a secondary dominant.

It was then cool to see the diminished chord in measure 31, since I don't know that. That's something we've talked about much, and I didn't see it in any of the other examples, but I liked that. It was cool to see the scale in measure 29 that was in opposite directions.

And I also thought that the harmonies overall were pretty good and I liked seeing the variation in the bass line, seeing a mix of the Alberti bass, the octaves, chords, and rhythmic variation with both quarter notes and eighth notes. So overall I was quite impressed with this one

I think this one has a lot of potential right now. There are a lot of double sharps showing up throughout the whole thing that read weird and sound weird. It seems to me to be the case also that when a high C sharp above the staff is put in, the music notates at an octave higher than intended.

And so that's a mistake that we need to try to fix. I think if we can fix those, then this one could potentially have room to be my favorite. I think it does a good job with the sequence and repetition like the other ones do.

And I think that some of the arpeggio patterns in the right hand and the way that it interacts with the left hand feels fairly mature. I think it's pretty good. It's just got the notational issues that need to be corrected

This one was pretty good. I thought it did a good job using the sequence and repetition throughout. I was impressed with this. I didn't love measures 9 through 12.

I felt like the pattern of playing a triad and then doing a descending 5-finger pattern down and back up was kind of weird. I don't know. I guess it was different in measures 10 and 12, so maybe that's a unique difference and a variation that I missed originally.

But still, I didn't necessarily love that part, and I felt like the harmonic progression of going from the B minor chord in measure 11 to the B dominant 7 specifically, I felt like that was weird. I can see what it's trying to do to modulate and give a secondary dominant to E. But I didn't love the way that it did it similarly in measure 14.

I thought it was cool in 31 having the scale in opposite directions. That was fun, and that does feel like a Mozart thing to me

I quite liked this one. There were some parts that didn't feel quite like Mozart to me, but honestly for the most part it felt pretty good and I I really liked it. Um it is cool to see the variation in the types of bass patterns both in rhythm and going between triads to the octaves, so that was cool.

I was honestly quite impressed with the 16th note runs and arpeggios. I thought those actually showed quite a bit of musical maturity. And I was also a big fan of the sequence and repetition repetition um all throughout. It felt really cool to hear kind of each you know, it wasn't necessarily a ton of s sequence and repetition that was consistent throughout the entire piece, but each you know eight bar phrase had its own sequence and repetition that I think I really liked. 

Also, I really enjoyed the dotted quarter followed by two sixteenths patternthat we saw in bars 30 and 23

This one was also alright. It was mostly pretty good, but there were some parts that just didn't feel quite in character or quite correct to me. For example, the 16th note runs in measures 9 through 11 felt kind of weird. Especially the harmony in measure 11 I didn't really love.

I can see how it's trying to be a circle of fifths progression 9 through 12 and leading into the modulation. But something about it didn't feel quite right. Similarly, measure 29, the 16th note runs didn't feel quite like a Mozart thing to me, and they're maybe a little more awkward to play, but overall this was pretty good

This one was pretty good. I was impressed with the melody, although there were some parts that I did feel were a little bit weird, such as measure 10. I don't know the harmonic motion of that didn't quite work for me. I don't know.

Overall, it was pretty good. Some of the sixteenth note runs, like for example on Measure 25, it didn't feel very Mozart-esque to me, but I don't know. Overall, it was pretty good. There were just some things in the harmony, a couple spots that didn't feel quite right

Wow, I'm impressed with the use of the contrapuntal sequences and voices. It's actually quite impressive to see the repetition of a same motif but carried out in the different lines. This feels very much like actual Bach writing, and the alternating between the left and right hand with the eighth note melody versus the quarter and eighth note accompaniment, or sorry, I meant the sixteenth note running melody.

Anyways, I thought the chord progression was very good, and it made good use of the secondary dominance, like Bach actually does. Fugs like this are a little bit more difficult to play, and so it's a little bit harder for me to comment on playability, but it feels to me like this really is quite playable, which is impressive.

I don't know that I have any feedback right now on how to improve. However, I'm no expert on Bach, and so it's hard for me to give super useful feedback on something like this

I came back and listened to this one again, and honestly, it was quite impressive. I think it has a lot of the really good qualities of all of these, such as the contrabandal voicing, the naturally moving between the major and minor modes in the key, the secondary dominance.

I think it did a great job with the sequence and repetition. I really loved the line, measures 3 to 4 with the baseline repeating that, and then honestly, I really like this. I think this is probably my favorite.

And then the ending felt very tasteful to me too, because it was a perfect authentic cadence. Ending with the leading tone going up to the root, which feels very true and authentic to me, and the 16th note pickup into the downbeat of the last chord felt great to me.

Honestly, I think this is my favorite musically

This one feels like it's sort of got the same type of contrapuntal multi-voice style, but it doesn't feel like it's quite as much like Bach as other parts do. Some of the melodic choices are really strange. I think the worst of them is in measure twelve going from the A to the D sharp, from beat 3 to beat 4, that is a crime in box time to have a tritone in the melody like that.

And you would never see something like that, and it sounds really weird. Also, much of this just feels like arpeggios with a on a changing chord progression. And so it feels more like some modern pop musician playing on a chord progression but trying to improvise in the style of Bach and doing so badly.

Overall, this is not my favorite, and I'm not very impressed with this one

I was not a big fan of this one. It also seems like on paper it checks all of the boxes. You know, it has a little bit of the contrapuntal voicing and some of the sequence and repetition, but you know so much of it just feels like it's trying to check boxes and it's not doing it in a good way.

In the middle section, bars 7 through 9, it has some ties, which I think are common in Bach fuges, but it's it feels more like a syncopation, which is not the right style, and so many of the chords and the arpeggio over the chord just feel very basic and they don't feel very Bach like.

Again, it sounds like somebody badly trying to improvise over a chord progression in the style of Bach, but they don't really know what Bach sounds like. They just know what contrapuntal voicing is. And some of the non-chord tones, especially in the beginning, which I guess really there's not that many non-chord tones, but I didn't feel like the harmonic progression really made proper use of secondary dominance or non-diatonic chords in the way that Bach would.

And so this one didn't feel very good to me

This one felt more on the mark to me. I think the thing that impressed me was the way that it switched between the major and minor modes in this key. I thought it was really cool to hear it go between those so easily and how it used secondary dominance so naturally.

I think that was really impressive to me. There were some parts where the chords still felt pretty basic and it felt like we were sticking very much to the chord tones and not quite giving some of the famous tension that Bach is known for, but overall I think this is a big improvement from the previous two

This one did pretty well. I was also impressed with the ability to switch between the major and minor modes in this key and the use of secondary dominants. Some of the secondary dominant patterns were maybe reused or repeated. And it was, you know, fairly common circle of fifths progression, but that felt true to me and that felt well like representative of the style.

And it felt interesting and kept me engaged and so I liked this one. Again, it did a good job with the contrapuntal voicing. I think each of these seemed to do a good job with that part. This one didn't blow my socks off, but it didn't suck.

It was actually pretty good

Wow, I really liked this one. This one might be a candidate for my favorite. I thought it did a really good job with the repetition of the same motif being used from the beginning clear to the very end. I don't know that the others were quite as consistent about that, and I thought that was really cool, but it was also cool to see that it reused motif in a different key.

And so that stuck out to me. I liked that a lot. I also really liked the section measures 12 through 14. Hearing that descending bass line and you know it was a very simple sequence and repetition, but it was executed quite well and you know almost tastefully rather than just like something that it was trying to check off a box.

And it actually sounded good and I think it really worked. It was measures 12 through 14. That was impressive to me

I genuinely enjoyed listening to this. This was really fun. Actually, I think the use of syncopation was maybe a little bit much. There's perhaps a little bit more syncopation than I'm used to hearing.

Or maybe it was just that some of the syncopation was a little different than how I typically hear it. I think sometimes it seemed like the last note of the phrase would end on a sixteenth offbeat, which I think is a little bit atypical in this type of music.

But overall, I really loved the structure. I thought it was a very clear delineation between the A section and the B section. I don't know that they have the same number of measures between the two phrases, which is an important aspect of ragtime.

I think it's worth checking on that. I'm trying to count real quick, but anyways, it's pretty close, I think. It might, you know, it might actually be the same. No, it's not. The A section is definitely longer by a handful of measures, which I think is an issue.

But aside from that, though, this is pretty good. I loved the difference in the key, or at least the way it sounds in the B section. I thought that was really mature, and the use of blue notes felt really appropriate to me, so I liked this

This one was fun. I could really see myself enjoying playing this one and think that I could use it. I actually really liked it. I thought it did a great job with the diminished chords and with the secondary dominance.

Those actually felt really quite tasteful to me. The syncopation felt more natural, but maybe I'm just accustomed to the way that Claude is writing it now. Maybe not. Either way, I thought this was pretty good. The one exception was that it didn't really end on an authentic cadence.

It had the leading tone and the second to last note and the melody, which was great, but then the left-hand chord was the root chord. And it was in second inversion, so it could have very easily been a dominant chord to bring it home, and it didn't do that.

And so that's pretty much the main piece of feedback that I'd give for this one

Man, this one was a bop. That was really fun. I again was really impressed with the use of secondary dominance in this one. At the beginning, the secondary dominant of the 5 was used to bring it into the tonality of C major and then bring it back to resolve into F. Some of the secondary dominants were used to move into the relative minor, which really impressed me.

Anyways, the secondary dominant usage in this was great, along with the diminished chords. I thought those were again very good. I really liked the stretch in 25, 26, and 27. The 16th note pattern on the right hand was really fun, actually, kind of giving it a syncopated feel, yet having a note on every beat.

That was really cool. I also liked in 29 through 31 when it started to use the chords in the right hand to complement the melody, moving in thirds, moving along the chord tones. I really liked that. This was a really fun one. Appreciated that this was the only one to use the modally borrowed minor iv chord.

This one was really pretty good too. I loved everything harmonically about it. And I loved the rhythmic pattern that was used, for example, in measures 21 to 23, and then again in measures 29 to 31. It was the same as in the previous song.

The sixteenth notes grouped into the different rhythms of a pattern of three, three and two. I thought that was really fun. The syncopation in this one didn't feel quite right. It felt like many of the measures had the exact same rhythm, and so it just felt really kind of repetitive, and the rhythm was a little bit awkward. Hard and unwieldy, and so it made the rest of the piece feel a little unwieldy as it kept repeating that rhythmic motif.

And so it could use some work there, but aside from that, there were a lot of things going really well for this one

I especially liked the blue notes in it and the occasional use of chords in the right hand. Felt fun.

This one was really fun. Again, made great use of the harmonies and followed the rhythm rules. I loved the diminished chords in this one. I think I liked the B section the most because of the way that it used the chords in the right hand.

I thought that was really fun, and I loved the chromaticism in the bass. The A section was fun, and the melody was great, but again, the syncopation in the melody just didn't quite sit right in the A section. But the B section, the syncopation actually felt really good

This one was a little bit more difficult and bland to listen to. I could see that it checked a lot of the boxes in terms of the theory, and I think it actually did a pretty decent job of using secondary dominance and some of the diminished chords.

But there was something about the melody that just didn't catch my attention. It was also cool to see how it tried to mimic an introduction from ragtime music in the first two measures. I thought that was nice. I thought it was kind of a boring introduction as far as ragtime introductions go.

And so I didn't like that introduction specifically, but it was cool to see that this model tried to do that. But yeah, the descending octave chromatic notes wasn't really that exciting
